text: The manor gets an outside before anything else outdoors: roofs, gables where the garret's gable windows are, chimney stacks where the flues rise, stone-slate and gritstone, glass, and a far stand-in, all generated from the same plan. Today it is a flat-capped carved block.

Story geography in one coordinate frame: the manor and London are not placed 150 km apart, nor joined by a portal, but by a declared compressed journey (the drive, a lane over a crest and down a hollow way, the suburb thickening into a street at a bar). Each change of look happens where the view is blocked (a crest, a bend, the houses closing in).

Stream the manor first: before outdoors, the existing house is built in workers and uploaded in time-sliced pieces, nearest first, and judged by the worst frame at each crossing on the phone (not by average fps), so the outdoors arrives into a pipeline already shown not to hitch.

One world-space authority: the ground you stand on, what is solid, claims and doorways become world-space queries in layers (terrain, forecourt, the house's floors and stairs), which the walker, the placer, the checks and the renderer all ask; meshes are projections of them. Not 'terrain plus the existing house'.
